subject: Adding extra solvent molecules to a membrane-protein system

messages.author: Bhattacharjee, Sinjini
messages.body:
Dear Amber users,
I want to replace a single protein chain with extra TIP3P waters, in a protein-lipid-bilayer box (generated using packmol-memgen).
Can this be done using tleap without affecting the the original lipids?
Any help or suggestions will be appreciated.
Best ,

messages.author: Stephan Schott
messages.body:
Hi Sinjini,
Is the system already simulated somehow, and that's why you want to replace a single chain? Otherwise, repacking everything would be probably easier.
This method could be a bit hacky, but here it goes (and seems more complicated than it is). It could also help someone else to get creative with such cases:
If you want to do this, it is probably easier done with packmol itself. Pdbremix gives you information regarding the volume of the protein in the different sections of your system. You can get this information by making a dummy run of packmol-memgen with the chain you want to remove.
Make a folder and place a pdb with the chain extracted from your packed system. Run it with something like --solvate --notrun, and see the volume in the packmol-memgen.log logfile. From there you can get how many water molecules you'd have to add (you can roughly estimate 0.033 waters per cubic angstrom), and a packmol.inp template file. Edit the template packmol.inp, change the number of waters for what you calculated, the coordinates in "inside box" to cover the simulation system where you want to replace the protein chain, and replace PROT0.pdb with your system without the chain you want to replace. You might want to check if you need to add ions for the removed charges of the protein chain you erased. Run packmol with "packmol < packmol.inp", it should be rather fast (make sure to run charmmlipid2amber -i packedpdb -o packedpdb, I think I still use a non-amber TIP3P pdb, and that should replace it). Check the packed structure, but all (or most) water molecules should have been added to the pocket that was left. Then you can load the generated system in leap to reparametrize it (without solvating of course). Just consider setting the PBC with "set XXX box {X Y Z}" according to the size of the original system, where XXX is the name of the loaded pdb object.
Hope it helps somehow,
Stephan Schott Verdugo

messages.author: Todd Minehardt
messages.body:
Sinjini,
I see there is already a detailed approach but here is what I was going to
suggest:
(1) Take your system PDB and manually remove the protein chain from it,
save that file;
(2) Run tLEaP as you did before, only use the saved file without the
protein chain in the loadpdb step; and
(3) Make sure you change the names of the prmtop and crd files, you should
now have your system with water (and maybe counterions, too) where the
protein chain was before.
Cheers,
Todd
